claims.text: Controlled thermal annealing can enhance short-range chemical order in multi-component concentrated alloys.
Enhanced short-range chemical order generates local lattice distortions.
Short-range-order-induced lattice distortions impede dislocation motion.
Impeded dislocation motion increases yield strength.
Enhanced short-range chemical order alters deformation and failure behavior.
The homogenized initial alloy has a primarily random atomic distribution and minimal pre-existing short-range order.
Annealing can induce short-range chemical order while maintaining overall composition and other microstructural features.
Significant atomic-size mismatch and favorable mixing enthalpies permit short-range order to develop in single-phase concentrated alloys.
Short-range ordered atomic clusters produce mismatch stress fields.
Mismatch stress fields associated with ordered regions hinder dislocation glide.
Annealed samples with greater short-range order will have a statistically significant increase in yield strength relative to a rapidly quenched random baseline.
Annealed samples with greater short-range order will exhibit altered dislocation pile-ups or reduced dislocation mobility relative to the baseline.
As-solidified or rapidly quenched concentrated alloys provide a random atomic baseline with minimal short-range order.
The proposed mechanism is expected to hold when the alloy is single-phase and deformation is dominated by dislocations.
The influence of short-range order should be weaker when atomic-size differences are minimal.
The influence of short-range order should be less marked when grain-boundary or precipitate strengthening dominates.
The magnitude of strengthening and detailed deformation response depend on alloy composition and annealing parameters.
